facts.fact: The authors' review states that the National eHealth Strategy was formally adopted in March 2020, to be implemented between 2020 and 2024, and that it lists establishing a home-grown EHR for Botswana inside a national eHealth platform by 2023 as a strategic intervention.
The authors quote the National eHealth Strategy, adopted in March 2020, as stating that all public hospitals have an electronic medical record that is real time; no count of hospitals is given.

A survey of health ICT staff run from 24 September 2019 to 23 March 2020 found that the public clinics surveyed (three respondents, in Gaborone, Francistown and Maun) accessed the Integrated Patient Management System, as did all the public hospitals surveyed (four respondents); the sites were chosen because eRecord systems are used in those districts.

The authors quote the March 2020 National eHealth Strategy as saying the public hospitals' electronic medical record is real time, and report from their 2019-20 survey that most eRecord systems are not interoperable within or between facilities, that there is no national unique patient identifier, and that patients hold duplicate electronic and paper records.

note: No HMIS fact: DHIS is named as accessed at public hospitals with no description of what it reports. IPMS is classed emr on the paper's statement that public facilities use eRecord systems for patient record management. The digitised value rests on the strategy's words 'real time' and is the weakest of the four; the paper states plainly that the record is not shared. The survey's public hospitals are not typed by tier, so the survey's tiers fact carries only the clinics. Not recorded as facts: the ministry cutting 37 eRecord systems to nine in 2013, which covers every class, and 'unclear ownership of eHealth', one interviewee's remark. Tables 1 to 3 are missing from the stored text. The paper's day of publication is not given; the facts are dated to the strategy and the survey.
